one_line: Chaulukya king Bhima II and his Vaghela general Lavanaprasada defend and rebuild Gujarat after the 1197 Ghurid sack.

appearance.age_look: Bhima II appears in his late thirties with a regal but slightly weary medium build; Lavanaprasada appears in his early thirties, taller and more athletic.
appearance.face: Both have oval faces and medium-brown Gujarati complexions; Bhima II has softer features, a neatly groomed moustache, faint under-eye lines and a calm yet burdened expression, while Lavanaprasada has a sharper jaw, a more angular nose, a thicker moustache and a focused, determined gaze; both default to a serious, dignified expression with subtle intensity in the eyes.
appearance.hair: Bhima II’s black hair is oiled and drawn into a low knot at the back, partly hidden beneath a simple golden cloth turban with a narrow red band; Lavanaprasada’s black hair is tied into a higher warrior’s knot at the back of the head, with no turban, and a narrow red cloth band around his forehead to keep hair off his face.
appearance.costume: Bhima II wears a long, knee-length golden-yellow silk angarkha with side-tie fastening and a subtle woven floral pattern, over a deep-red cotton dhoti wrapped to the ankles with a broad pleated front, a cream-bordered red silk patka (waist sash) knotted at his left hip, and a light cream shawl draped from his left shoulder across his torso; he has simple gold stud earrings, a short multi-strand gold necklace, a thin gold armlet on each upper arm, and plain leather sandals; Lavanaprasada wears a fitted, quilted dark-indigo cotton coat of mail-style padded jerkin reaching mid-thigh, worn over a lighter indigo cotton tunic, with a plain off-white dhoti tied slightly shorter for movement, a brick-red cotton patka wound tightly at the waist, and a practical brown leather belt; over his jerkin he has a plain steel breastplate with a slightly raised central boss, simple steel bracers on his forearms, a round wooden shield slung on his back, and sturdy dark-brown leather sandals; both are fully and modestly clothed in era-appropriate draped garments covering torso and legs.
appearance.signature: Bhima II carries a ceremonial straight-bladed steel sword with a simple Gujarati-style cross-guard and a brown leather scabbard, its hilt wrapped in deep-red cord, while Lavanaprasada wields a practical steel talwar with a slightly curved blade and disc pommel, its plain brown scabbard hanging from his belt.

ref_desc: Bhima II has an oval medium-brown face, low-knotted black hair under a simple golden turban, a golden-yellow silk angarkha over a deep-red dhoti with cream shawl and a ceremonial straight steel sword, while Lavanaprasada has sharper features, a higher warrior’s knot, a dark-indigo quilted jerkin with steel breastplate over an off-white dhoti, brick-red sash and a practical curved steel talwar, all in golden yellow, deep red, cream, dark indigo and brown leather tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two Gujarati figures from c. 1200 CE standing side by side: Bhima II as a dignified king and Lavanaprasada as his warrior-general. Bhima II has an oval medium-brown face, calm but slightly burdened eyes, a neat moustache and black hair oiled into a low knot, partly covered by a simple golden cloth turban with a narrow red band; he wears a knee-length golden-yellow silk angarkha with subtle woven floral pattern, over a deep-red cotton dhoti wrapped to his ankles with a broad pleated front, a cream-bordered red silk patka knotted at his left hip, a light cream shawl draped from his left shoulder, simple gold stud earrings, a short multi-strand gold necklace, thin gold armlets on both upper arms, plain leather sandals, and carries a ceremonial straight-bladed steel sword with a simple Gujarati cross-guard and brown leather scabbard, its hilt wrapped in deep-red cord. Lavanaprasada stands slightly behind and to the side, taller and more athletic, with a sharper jaw and medium-brown complexion, thick moustache, focused intense eyes and black hair tied into a higher warrior’s knot, held back by a narrow red cloth band around his forehead; he wears a fitted quilted dark-indigo cotton jerkin reaching mid-thigh over a lighter indigo tunic, a plain off-white dhoti tied slightly shorter for movement, a brick-red cotton patka tightly wound at the waist, a plain steel breastplate with a raised central boss over the jerkin, simple steel bracers on his forearms, a round wooden shield slung on his back, sturdy dark-brown leather sandals, and at his left side a slightly curved steel talwar with disc pommel in a plain brown scabbard. Keep both figures fully and modestly clothed in historically plausible Gujarati garments, emphasize the golden yellow, deep red, cream, dark indigo and brown leather palette, and show them in a neutral stance suitable for consistent redrawing, with clear views of face, hair, clothing and weapons.
